sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: About 4000 BCE onwards, Sindhu-Sarasvatī developed techniques of wheel- turned pottery production, pigmentation, application of protective or decorative coats (called ‘slips’) of multiple colours, decorative painting, etc.
sections.source_evidence: About 4000 BCE onwards, Sindhu-Sarasvatī developed techniques of wheel- turned pottery production, pigmentation, application of protective or decorative coats (called ‘slips’) of multiple colours, decorative painting, etc.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: These techniques became further sophisticated during the Sindhu-Sarasvatī (also known as ‘Harappan’) Civilisation (2600–1900 BCE), with a bright red surface painted with black-coloured designs displaying geometric patterns, and aquatic and terrestrial animals.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: The clay used for making pots, dishes, bowls and other items was carefully selected and cleaned, sieved, kneaded, turned over a wheel and finally baked in kilns (baked clay is called ‘terracotta’).
